# dsh-session-monitor

DeepSeek Harness shows one conversation at a time. While several sessions work in
parallel, the side

bar tells you *that* a session is running or waiting — the
question itself, the turn it is in, and t

he message it wants to send stay behind
its own row. This plugin adds **Session Monitor** to the lef

## Picking this up elsewhere

This directory carries a HANDOFF.md: current state, the architecture and its exact
data sources, the

liveness heuristics, what was verified, what was not, pitfalls, and the next
steps. Read it before

## The grid

- **Which sessions.** Every non-blank root session in the client catalog.
Subagent child rows and th

e provisional New Session row are not conversations
a person monitors here — except the blank sessio

n this toolbar just created,
whose card is exactly what the user asked for until its first turn titl

es it.
- **The order freezes once cards are on screen.** The grid seeds its order one
time (waiting,

then running, then recency) and then stores it in `localStorage`.
After that, a prompt, a new turn

or a state change updates a card's content but
never its position — a session that becomes the most

recently active does not
jump to the front, and leaving the panel or restarting the app resumes the

same
cells instead of re-seeding them. A card keeps its position until it is the
**oldest** card and

a new session needs that slot: the newcomer takes that exact
cell and the displaced card waits at t

he order's tail. A session that appears
later joins at the end while there is room. A waiting card i

s never displaced. A
session created by this toolbar follows the same rule, so starting one never
re

shuffles the page.
- **Activity never reorders the grid.** A prompt, a new turn or a state change
up

dates a card's content, never its position. The one deliberate exception is
a smaller card budget: l

owering it re-seeds the grid, so the cards that stay
on screen are the **newest** sessions, arranged

newest-first. Raising the
budget keeps that order and reveals the rest in place.
- **Card budget.**

The toolbar's **Cards** stepper moves the budget one card at
a time, from **2** up to **24** (defau

lt 9), for idle and running sessions. The
number in the middle is editable, and a value typed outsid

e the range is
normalised when the field is left. A session **waiting for the user is never cut
off

by the budget** — it is the reason the panel exists.
- **Cards per row.** The toolbar's **Per row**

control sets an exact count (2–6)
or leaves the grid on **Auto**, which fills the column with 260px

cards. The
choice is remembered beside the removed ids.
- **Removal.** Removed ids are stored in thi

s browser's `localStorage`

## How it reads and acts

The plugin is browser-only in behaviour. It registers one sidebar row, one `main`
panel, and two loc

ale dictionaries — no host route, no tool, no event listener —
because every fact it needs already e
xists in the client:
| Fact | Source |

| session identity, title, workspace path, recency, run-state fallback | `ctx.sessions.list` |
| Wor

kspace title shown on the card | `ctx.workspaces.list` |
| pending question / approval | `ctx.uiSess

ion.sessionStatus` |
| live run state of one card | `binding.session.getSnapshot().running` |
| live

transcript | `ctx.sessions.retain()` → `binding.eventSource` |
| send a prompt | `binding.session.p

rompt(content, 'queue')` |
| answer a pending request | the carrier's own `answer()` |
| current per

mission preset | `binding.session.projections.faceOf('permissions')` |
| selectable permission prese

ts | `ctx.remote.permissionPresets.catalog()` |
| switch the preset | `binding.session.command('/per

mission <preset>')` |
| queued messages | `binding.session.projections.faceOf('inbox')` → `next-turn

` |
| steer / edit / discard a queued message | `binding.session.updateQueue(id, { kind: 'steer' \|

'edit' \| 'remove' })` |
| stop the running turn | `binding.session.cancel()` |
| open the session |

`ctx.uiWorkspace.openSession(sessionId)` |
| current model and catalog | `ctx.modelDirectories.dire

ctoryFor(sessionId)` |
| switch the model | the same directory's `select({ provider, model })` |
| c
reate a session in place | `ctx.sessions.create({ workspaceId })` (fallback `ctx.uiWorkspace.connect

Workspace`) |
| keep a created blank session as a card | the monitor's local `spawned` set in `local

Storage` |
| adopt a folder as a Workspace | `ctx.workspaces.create({ path })` |
| ask for a folder
| `ctx.remote.directoryPicker.pick()` |
